defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: Dedup removes new_m before confirming old_m exists; if old_m is absent, ValueError is raised and new_m is dropped from the scene (lines 37-38)
replace(A, A) removes A before the search, raising ValueError and leaving A removed (line 37)
Nit: dedup only checks the current list level, so nested duplicates of new_m are not caught (line 37)
votes.evidence_quote: When `old_mobject is new_mobject` (same identity), line 37's `new_m in mobj_list` is `True`, so line 38 removes the object before the search loop finds it, turning a harmless no-op into a `ValueError` that corrupts state.
votes.justification: The review's second finding matches the known defect at the dedup in replace_in_list. It names the cause: removal happens before the search. It gives the input replace(A, A) and the symptoms: ValueError raised and A dropped from the scene.
